answer: Anchor each agent identity to a distinct, aged domain it controls via a DNS TXT challenge, one identity per domain. Domains cost fees, take time to age, and bulk buys leave registrar trails, so a sybil farmer pays cash and waits for every fake. Like dawn over a tundra, the proof is public: anyone can re-check the record, and the echo of that check reaches every peer. Re-verification revokes identities whose domains lapse, and standing grows only after the domain survives several epochs. Each clone needs a funded, aged domain, so mass identity becomes slow, expensive and auditable.
